| tsk-p7-shadow-binders | Retire the two remaining self-verifying shadow binders in `src/runner/dispatch/placement-policy.mjs` (`resolveVerifiedPlacementModel`) and `src/runner/dispatch/provider-adapter.mjs` (`resolveVerifiedProviderArgs`) — dispatch-engine-liveness-hardening Phase 7 (C1) investigated both and found real, if now near-zero, historical production divergence (not near-zero for two OTHER shadow binders in the same audit finding, which Phase 7 already deleted outright since their own two sides always called the identical primitive with identical inputs). Kept these two in shadow mode rather than retiring, with durable local telemetry added (`recordShadowBinderDivergence`, `.fgos/dispatch/shadow-binder-divergence.jsonl`, surfaced by the `shadow-binder-divergence` doctor check) so a future retirement decision has real evidence instead of the ephemeral-stderr-only visibility this phase found (had to manually grep ~800 historical `.fgos/assignments/*/runs/*/stderr.log` files to find the one real divergence window this phase traced). Target: 2026-10-31, or sooner once enough durable telemetry accumulates to re-evaluate. Enumerated divergence classes still open, each needing a decided winner + a matrix test in `test/runner/placement-policy-matrix-coverage.test.mjs`/`test/runner/provider-adapter.test.mjs` before flipping: (a) `resolveVerifiedPlacementModel` — an executor with no declared `providerModel` defaults to `claude`'s model table on the legacy side (`resolve.mjs`'s `modelForTier`) but derives its real family via `deriveProviderFamily` on the PlacementPolicy side; (b) `resolveVerifiedPlacementModel` — an `executors.<id>.model` literal is read by PlacementPolicy's `buildPlacementPolicyCandidate` but ignored by the legacy `modelForTier` formula (masked today only because `cli.mjs`'s `executeExecutorCli` re-applies `executor?.model` as an explicit override after the binder returns; NOT masked in `spawnWorker`, a real live gap); (d) `resolveVerifiedPlacementModel`/C3's `cfg.models` dual-keying — with no `cfg.modelPolicies` table present, the legacy path reads `cfg.models` keyed by WORK tier (light/standard/heavy) while `resolvePolicyTierModel` reads the SAME field keyed by POLICY tier (lightweight/standard/.../critical); real production config always declares `modelPolicies` today (confirmed: `.fgos/config.json` has both `modelPolicies` and a flat `models` key), so this is dormant for this repo's own dispatch but live for any consuming project whose config omits `modelPolicies`; (i) `resolveVerifiedProviderArgs` — an executor's args template with no `{model}` placeholder and no literal `--model` gets `--model <resolved>` appended by `ClaudeProviderAdapter.render()` but nothing appended by the legacy string-substitution path (the ONLY class with real historical production evidence: 126 confirmed real divergences, all dated 2026-09-18, root-caused to a since-fixed `.fgos/config.json` args-template gap — re-verified empirically against every currently-registered production claude-family executor invocation on 2026-09-29: 0/5 diverge today); (ii) `resolveVerifiedProviderArgs` — a combined `--model=value` argv form (not the separate `'--model', 'value'` token pair every currently-registered executor actually uses) would not be detected by the adapter's `renderedArgs.includes('--model')` check, causing a spurious double `--model` append; unexercised by any currently-registered executor, but a real gap the adapter's own check needs a `startsWith('--model=')` branch to close before that specific binder could ever be made unconditionally authoritative. | Each of the 5 enumerated classes above has a decided winner (legacy or PlacementPolicy/ProviderAdapter) backed by a real matrix test, OR the `cfg.models` dual-keying gap (class d) is fixed directly; once all classes are closed, `resolveVerifiedPlacementModel`/`resolveVerifiedProviderArgs` retire the same way the other two shadow binders already did in this same phase (call the target function directly, delete the legacy fallback computation) | proposed | dispatch-engine-liveness-hardening |

## 3. Typed operations

All mutations require operation id, validated repository, writer and **declared resource set + existing authority**. No option-bag escape to raw Git args. Reads are bounded/paginated and do not repair. Doctor never mutates.

| Port | Operations and guarantees |
|---|---|
| Inspect | resolveRepo/Ref, status, diff, ancestry, readObjects, pathsAtRevision (batched), listWorktrees, compareContent, snapshotWrites; explicit unknown/error and byte-safe paths; every Inspect call runs with optional locks off (`--no-optional-locks`), because `status` otherwise refreshes the index under `index.lock` |
| Refs | ensureBranch, advanceRef, deleteRef, fastForwardCheckedOut; exact-old CAS, never blind `branch -D`. Exact-old CAS does **not** protect a checked-out branch (`update-ref -d` deleted the current branch in the Git floor proof, and the V-CAS re-check deleted a branch that a worktree registered after the snapshot had checked out): every Refs mutation of `refs/heads/*` takes worktree-admin 40 (§5), and under that one hold revalidates every registered checkout (main and linked; a symbolic HEAD to an unborn name counts as checked out), performs the exact-old CAS, reads back the ref and the registered checkouts, and only then releases 40, so no fgOS worktree registration can come between the check and the effect. An earlier snapshot of checkout membership protects nothing. An in-use ref is refused. No typed operation switches the branch of an existing checkout; one added later takes 40 first. A switch by raw Git or a worker is outside the concurrency guarantee (§9) and is reported as `recovery-required` when that read-back sees it. The one exception is `fastForwardCheckedOut(branch, expectedOld, next)`: fast-forward only, exact-old CAS, the branch is checked out only in a worktree whose verified `dispatch-cwd` lease the caller holds, that checkout is clean, and its tree is updated under that custody; anything else is refused |
| Worktree | create, createDetached, relocate, remove, inspectOrphans, repairRegistration; one admin door, no rm-rf fallback. Git returns after registration/strip of worker `.fgos`; provisioning is Execution. |
| ScopedCommit | preflight/commit; foreign index refusal, custody, literal exact selection, postcommit set/tree proof. A tracked file move is a ScopedCommit with both literal paths (old deleted, new added); failure restores both paths to their immediately pre-commit existence, mode and content before any consumer registry update (a producer move already made before commit remains old-absent/new-present); there is no separate file-move operation |
| Sync | start/inspect/continue/abort; pinned target, scoped resolver, operation-owned merge state |
| Land | prepare/publish/recover; immutable candidate, merge or squash, journalled CAS/checkout. Consumer supplies verification evidence. |
| SafeRestore | preview/apply/recover/listSnapshot/extractPath/acknowledge; full locked checks and durable snapshot before destructive effect. `apply` may carry `reapplyLocalDelta`: after the snapshot and the restore to the new tip, the captured local delta is applied to index and tree; a failed reapply leaves the durable snapshot and returns `recovery-required` (replaces `resyncWorktree`'s `reset --hard` + `apply --index`) |
| Checkpoint adapter | checkpointTrackedFiles; detachable, consumer-selected **non-event** tracked payload only |
| RepositoryConfig | publicationFetchMappings(remote), ensureFetchMapping, ensureHooks, removeOwnedHooksConfig; local config, user settings preserved, provenance |
| Remote | fetchRefs, pushRefs, inspectRemote; explicit mapping, no implicit all-refs or default push-config mutation |
| Recovery | inspectOperation, listPending, reconcile; actual disk/ref checks and idempotent results |
| Publication | restricted plumbing; section 4. Event Store is the only production writer of event refs |

Implementation may collapse ports internally; the appendix maps lessons to this surface. Idempotency is required wherever an effect can repeat.

Implementation checkpoint (2026-10-19, dormant): `src/git/refs.mjs` and `remote.mjs` marshal typed requests and explicit held handles, with no subprocess policy in Node. Refs uses worktree-admin 40 through membership revalidation, exact-old no-dereference CAS and read-back, and journals `RefUpdate`/`RefDelete` with a reachability pin and one TargetAttempt. `fastForwardCheckedOut` requires the exact registered worktree's rank-30 lease and a clean fast-forward. Non-event Remote takes literal source/destination pairs (fetch destinations under `refs/remotes/*`, push destinations under `refs/heads/*`), pins the granted remote URL, downloads objects before exact-old local CAS, and records `RemoteFetch`/`RemotePush` with per-target old/new values before TargetAttempt. Lost acknowledgements preserve the attempt and never resend that id. These ports have no production callers yet; unresolved operations preserve evidence and refuse replay. Linux files/reftable and local bare-remote proofs live in `packages/git/rust/tests/refs_remote.rs` and `test/git/{refs,remote,lock-handover}.test.mjs`. Separate-git-dir remains unsupported: inferred linked-cwd discovery requires a main `.git` directory and reciprocal registered admin/backlink, rather than trusting a worker gitfile alone.

2026-10-19 (phase 05 worktree, **not release-ready**): dormant ScopedCommit, non-event main Checkpoint and Sync ports now have Rust implementations and mechanical addon/Node bindings. ScopedCommit records baseline/ref/dirty-content fingerprints, stages literal NUL pathspecs, records a pre-OID TargetAttempt, and checks the actual committed tree and path set after one hook invocation. A contract violation retains the actual OID. Sync journals its pinned target and operation-owned conflict/staged sets, returns a temporary resolver grant, checks conflict markers before staging, and checks both merge parents. The cutover hook delegates to the activated host's protocol-1 `git-grant-check`; that read-only route verifies the inherited main-50 borrower, WAL description binding, unspent TargetAttempt, exact deletion paths, current legacy ref and seal digest. Every cutover also stages the `.fgos/events` fence when it is present as a regular file, replacing the deleted event directory or, in a baseline-only repository, marking the cutover. Linux-x64 activation now requires the native addon to declare `git-wal-v1`; old manifests still deserialize for a named refusal. Phase-05 unit 2 carries a real pre-open acquisition reach floor through the private Node handle and opaque loan, and the release/dev-host/test addon producer emits its platform capabilities. Sync records a durable `sync-commit-attempt` (prepared tree) immediately before invoking commit and refuses an uncertain attempt on resume, even when HEAD matches; its resulting ref is synced before the outcome. ScopedCommit and Sync receipt replay derive the actual committed path set from the immutable commit, preserving hook contract violations. Parent-death barriers and genuine temporary hook indexes have Linux fixture evidence. Unit 3 restores declared producer bytes from a transaction-local pre-staging snapshot after an observed rejection with unchanged HEAD, including both move paths, clean declared files, symlinks and modes; the initially empty index is restored even when the hook staged extra paths. Uncertain/crashed attempts retain the WAL and refuse replay rather than guessing rollback. Adopted setsid holders use the holder-lock descriptor rule below. Installed-release main cutover and unrestricted host/cross-platform acceptance remain outstanding. See [unit-2 report](../../../plans/reports/phase-lead-261019-1654-git-p05-u2-handover-reach-and-capability.md). The Node matcher and existing production commit/sync adapters remain for the planned phase-07 switch; no dormant port is an authorization to switch callers early.

2026-10-19 (landing repair): RepositoryConfig is the single source for publication fetch mappings. Event Store and Node setup/doctor read the Rust policy through the existing crate/addon boundary. The legacy mapping is `+refs/fgos/legacy*:refs/fgos/remotes/<remote>/legacy*`: Git permits an absent wildcard source, including before the cutover, and the empty suffix maps `refs/fgos/legacy` to exactly `refs/fgos/remotes/<remote>/legacy`. ensureFetchMapping replaces an installed old exact legacy mapping in the same journaled, native-config-lock-protected update, including when both forms exist; unrelated config and push settings remain untouched. Setup/doctor use `eventStore.remote` (project over global, registered setup default `origin`), and also detect and migrate obsolete exact mappings on `origin` when the configured remote differs. `obsolete_legacy_fetch_mapping` owns the obsolete form for every consumer; callers do not infer it by policy-list index. The wildcard reserves all `refs/fgos/legacy?*` names (any nonempty suffix): writers must never create them. Doctor reports any corresponding `refs/fgos/remotes/<remote>/legacy?*` mirrors, with source/mirror cleanup guidance; it never deletes these refs automatically.

2026-10-19 (review fixes): Untrusted repository URL rewrites (`url.*`, including `insteadOf` and `pushInsteadOf`) refuse before invocation. Remote overrides generic HTTP proxy, TLS verification, extra headers and redirect policy with safe values, and refuses other repository-local HTTP/HTTPS, SSH, credential, protocol and proxy overrides, including URL-scoped HTTP settings; trusted global transport configuration remains outside this repository boundary. Trust is determined by `git config --show-scope`: only system/global/command scopes are trusted; local/worktree and any unknown scope are untrusted, regardless of origin path spelling. Both the trusted main checkout and a linked handle’s worktree configuration are checked. Doctor’s `git-transport-config` reports refusing settings, including actions/checkout’s local `http.<url>.extraheader`; CI uses `persist-credentials: false` plus a trusted global credential helper or `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL`-level setting. Doctor never migrates secrets. Trusted global credential helpers remain available to Remote/Publication; preflight still refuses repository-local helpers, and the driver still scrubs inherited `GIT_*` overrides. SSH URLs may select a username (`ssh://git@host/path`); password/userinfo credentials are refused. Push uses `--atomic`, never forces, and classifies every destination from post-transfer observations; all unchanged destinations establish rejection, mixed observations remain unknown. Fetch refreshes remote-tracking refs with Git's default forced-update semantics, protected by exact-old no-dereference CAS; ancestry is not required. All destinations are checked before the first install. A stale destination or failed install with no local effect closes with a terminal not-acknowledged Transfer and per-target observations, without a pending operation id; readable partial installs close as unknown with observations. Unreadable outcomes retain recovery evidence and never replay. A failed fetch CAS does not stop the remaining destination installs; the final observations cover all destinations. A server without atomic push support produces a terminal Rejected outcome; there is no non-atomic fallback.

`fastForwardCheckedOut` refuses the trusted main checkout. Membership includes rebase-merge/rebase-apply `head-name` and `BISECT_START`; an ordinary user worktree lock does not make registration uncertain, while `locked initializing` does. Doctor `git-worktree-recovery` classifies a lock for inspection only (2026-10-19): a lock whose reason names `pid <N>` where process N is live and started no later than the lock file (pid plus start time, so a reused pid does not count) is `locked-by-live-process`, advisory like `dirty-or-stale-checkout-preserved`; a lock naming a dead, reused or unparseable owner stays `locked-registration` and fails the row. The reason text is read only for that pid token, never as authority for anything else, and nothing is unlocked or repaired. An explicit ignored-path/incoming-tree collision check preserves ignored content (Git 2.53 dry-run alone did not refuse the measured replacement). After index refresh, a dry-run two-tree `read-tree -m -n -u` must pass before TargetAttempt. A failed ref write which still observes the expected old tip is a write failure with recovery evidence, never a claimed CAS loss. RemoteFetch/RemotePush are the sole transfer WAL kinds, with explicit target old/new values for both Publication and non-event Remote; Publication retains its authority, expected/next and no-resend recovery rules. Historical Publication records without target detail deserialize with an empty target list for conservative recovery; all new writers emit the targets field and non-event transfers require a complete target set.

2026-10-19 (phase 03): Worktree uses the existing Rust LockScope, worktree-admin 40, Inspect topology, hardened driver, WAL admission/TargetAttempt and reachability pins. One hold spans identity/custody/status/proof checks and remove/move. Git children borrow admin authority; the caller's verified custody description stays pinned in the seeded scope until return. Remove preserves staged, unstaged, untracked, ignored and reappearing worker-state bytes, native locks, live cwd and unknown process facts; a process that exits during the cwd scan is re-observed through Process before treating its missing cwd as clear. A successful create strips worker `.fgos`; intentionally absent tracked state paths are marked skip-worktree in the new checkout's index, so later cleanup does not need an exemption for dirty paths. No provisioning callback runs in Git. Detached session allocation owns an `mkdtemp` directory and only attempts an empty-directory rollback before registration; registered cleanup always goes through non-force Git removal.

2026-10-19 (landing repair): A tracked, clean `.fgos` with no skip-worktree entries is not reappearing worker state and does not prevent Worktree removal or relocation.

2026-10-19 (phase 03 host gate): An unreadable cwd does not refuse remove or relocate; live same-user or unknown-owner processes with unreadable cwds produce a stderr warning naming pid and comm. A readable cwd inside or below the checkout still refuses. The caller's verified dispatch-cwd lease and refusal of another holder's lease cover fgOS producers; status checks preserve dirty or uncertain trees. Unreadability alone is not evidence that a process occupies this checkout.

2026-10-19 (phase 03 review): Allocation inside the trusted main checkout (including ignored `.claude/worktrees`) is supported; equal/ancestor paths, the common Git directory and nesting in linked checkouts remain refused. Readable cwd facts from any user protect a checkout; unreadable cwd facts are judged only for the effective user or unknown ownership. Privileged actors and unreadable foreign-user processes are outside this guarantee, so shared cross-user checkout custody is not certified. Same-user unreadability is advisory (see the host-gate policy below). Remove/move preflight refuses user locks and submodules and repeats custody/cwd checks immediately before TargetAttempt and the Git call. Removal additionally requires `deliveredTo` reachable from a surviving named non-`refs/fgos` ref; a detached tip alone is not delivery. Ignored bytes remain protected; ignored-directory inspection is collapsed with `--directory` and bounded by the Inspect output ceiling. Doctor reports preserved dirty/stale checkouts as advisory; pending operations, missing/locked registrations and partial/untrusted admin entries fail the row.

Under worktree-admin, after an attempted Git refusal or during repair, observable non-effects settle as terminal `Worktree { completed: false, details }` with the checked paths/registration observations, then release the candidate pin. Create requires absent registration and absent or empty owned destination; move requires absent destination plus unchanged admin identity, reciprocal source backlink and expected tip; remove requires that unchanged source state. This is record-only reconciliation under §10 rule 4, never a repeated attempt or a claim that an attempted operation was abandoned before attempt (§10 rule 4b). A replay of a false outcome returns a terminal refusal. Ambiguous residue remains pending and preserved.


Worktree WAL kinds bind canonical paths and registration names; move/remove additionally bind the admin directory's `dev:ino`, and remove binds the consumer's expected tip, delivery target and evidence digest. An established id is replayed without repeating its effect; pending attempts retain evidence. Recovery repairs a move only at its recorded destination and checks that destination's gitfile. An initializing create lock requires its own attempted WAL record, matching registration, branch and tip; a partial or dirty checkout stays preserved. Prune accepts only attempted WorktreeRemove evidence, a missing recorded checkout, the same admin inode and a matching backlink (or a partially removed backlink); it removes only the validated Git admin remainder, preserving unknown files, symlinks and native locks. It never invokes global prune or acquires custody. Four Linux x86_64 crash fixtures kill actual Git at ptrace syscall barriers; power-loss durability is not claimed.

`fgos worktree create <path> [--branch <name> | --detach] [--base <ref>] [--json]` is available now under the owner's plan Q2 answer of 2026-10-18. Without a branch it creates a detached checkout. Base accepts a full OID, HEAD or a literal branch/tag/remote ref. Other production Worktree callers migrate together in phase 07. `git-worktree-recovery` reads raw admin entries (including partial entries omitted by Git listing), dirty/stale checkouts and pending Worktree WAL records without repairing; phase 04 adds its producing-custody row to this same diagnostic.

The Node matcher and existing production commit/sync adapters remain for the planned phase-07 switch; no dormant port is an authorization to switch callers early.

2026-10-19 (landing repair): RepositoryConfig is the single source for publication fetch mappings. Event Store and Node setup/doctor read the Rust policy through the existing crate/addon boundary. The legacy mapping is `+refs/fgos/legacy*:refs/fgos/remotes/<remote>/legacy*`: Git permits an absent wildcard source, including before the cutover, and the empty suffix maps `refs/fgos/legacy` to exactly `refs/fgos/remotes/<remote>/legacy`. ensureFetchMapping replaces an installed old exact legacy mapping in the same journaled, native-config-lock-protected update, including when both forms exist; unrelated config and push settings remain untouched. Setup/doctor use `eventStore.remote` (project over global, registered setup default `origin`), and also detect and migrate obsolete exact mappings on `origin` when the configured remote differs. `obsolete_legacy_fetch_mapping` owns the obsolete form for every consumer; callers do not infer it by policy-list index. The wildcard reserves all `refs/fgos/legacy?*` names (any nonempty suffix): writers must never create them. Doctor reports any corresponding `refs/fgos/remotes/<remote>/legacy?*` mirrors, with source/mirror cleanup guidance; it never deletes these refs automatically.

2026-10-19 (review fixes): Untrusted repository URL rewrites (`url.*`, including `insteadOf` and `pushInsteadOf`) refuse before invocation. Remote overrides generic HTTP proxy, TLS verification, extra headers and redirect policy with safe values, and refuses other repository-local HTTP/HTTPS, SSH, credential, protocol and proxy overrides, including URL-scoped HTTP settings; trusted global transport configuration remains outside this repository boundary. Trust is determined by `git config --show-scope`: only system/global/command scopes are trusted; local/worktree and any unknown scope are untrusted, regardless of origin path spelling. Both the trusted main checkout and a linked handle’s worktree configuration are checked. Doctor’s `git-transport-config` reports refusing settings, including actions/checkout’s local `http.<url>.extraheader`; CI uses `persist-credentials: false` plus a trusted global credential helper or `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL`-level setting. Doctor never migrates secrets. Trusted global credential helpers remain available to Remote/Publication; preflight still refuses repository-local helpers, and the driver still scrubs inherited `GIT_*` overrides. SSH URLs may select a username (`ssh://git@host/path`); password/userinfo credentials are refused. Push uses `--atomic`, never forces, and classifies every destination from post-transfer observations; all unchanged destinations establish rejection, mixed observations remain unknown. Fetch refreshes remote-tracking refs with Git's default forced-update semantics, protected by exact-old no-dereference CAS; ancestry is not required. All destinations are checked before the first install. A stale destination or failed install with no local effect closes with a terminal not-acknowledged Transfer and per-target observations, without a pending operation id; readable partial installs close as unknown with observations. Unreadable outcomes retain recovery evidence and never replay. A failed fetch CAS does not stop the remaining destination installs; the final observations cover all destinations. A server without atomic push support produces a terminal Rejected outcome; there is no non-atomic fallback.

`fastForwardCheckedOut` refuses the trusted main checkout. Membership includes rebase-merge/rebase-apply `head-name` and `BISECT_START`; an ordinary user worktree lock does not make registration uncertain, while `locked initializing` does. Doctor `git-worktree-recovery` classifies a lock for inspection only (2026-10-19): a lock whose reason names `pid <N>` where process N is live and started no later than the lock file (pid plus start time, so a reused pid does not count) is `locked-by-live-process`, advisory like `dirty-or-stale-checkout-preserved`; a lock naming a dead, reused or unparseable owner stays `locked-registration` and fails the row. The reason text is read only for that pid token, never as authority for anything else, and nothing is unlocked or repaired. An explicit ignored-path/incoming-tree collision check preserves ignored content (Git 2.53 dry-run alone did not refuse the measured replacement). After index refresh, a dry-run two-tree `read-tree -m -n -u` must pass before TargetAttempt. A failed ref write which still observes the expected old tip is a write failure with recovery evidence, never a claimed CAS loss. RemoteFetch/RemotePush are the sole transfer WAL kinds, with explicit target old/new values for both Publication and non-event Remote; Publication retains its authority, expected/next and no-resend recovery rules. Historical Publication records without target detail deserialize with an empty target list for conservative recovery; all new writers emit the targets field and non-event transfers require a complete target set.

2026-10-19 (phase 03): Worktree uses the existing Rust LockScope, worktree-admin 40, Inspect topology, hardened driver, WAL admission/TargetAttempt and reachability pins. One hold spans identity/custody/status/proof checks and remove/move. Git children borrow admin authority; the caller's verified custody description stays pinned in the seeded scope until return. Remove preserves staged, unstaged, untracked, ignored and reappearing worker-state bytes, native locks, live cwd and unknown process facts; a process that exits during the cwd scan is re-observed through Process before treating its missing cwd as clear. A successful create strips worker `.fgos`; intentionally absent tracked state paths are marked skip-worktree in the new checkout's index, so later cleanup does not need an exemption for dirty paths. No provisioning callback runs in Git. Detached session allocation owns an `mkdtemp` directory and only attempts an empty-directory rollback before registration; registered cleanup always goes through non-force Git removal.

2026-10-19 (landing repair): A tracked, clean `.fgos` with no skip-worktree entries is not reappearing worker state and does not prevent Worktree removal or relocation.

2026-10-19 (phase 03 host gate): An unreadable cwd does not refuse remove or relocate; live same-user or unknown-owner processes with unreadable cwds produce a stderr warning naming pid and comm. A readable cwd inside or below the checkout still refuses. The caller's verified dispatch-cwd lease and refusal of another holder's lease cover fgOS producers; status checks preserve dirty or uncertain trees. Unreadability alone is not evidence that a process occupies this checkout.

2026-10-19 (phase 03 review): Allocation inside the trusted main checkout (including ignored `.claude/worktrees`) is supported; equal/ancestor paths, the common Git directory and nesting in linked checkouts remain refused. Readable cwd facts from any user protect a checkout; unreadable cwd facts are judged only for the effective user or unknown ownership. Privileged actors and unreadable foreign-user processes are outside this guarantee, so shared cross-user checkout custody is not certified. Same-user unreadability is advisory (see the host-gate policy below). Remove/move preflight refuses user locks and submodules and repeats custody/cwd checks immediately before TargetAttempt and the Git call. Removal additionally requires `deliveredTo` reachable from a surviving named non-`refs/fgos` ref; a detached tip alone is not delivery. Ignored bytes remain protected; ignored-directory inspection is collapsed with `--directory` and bounded by the Inspect output ceiling. Doctor reports preserved dirty/stale checkouts as advisory; pending operations, missing/locked registrations and partial/untrusted admin entries fail the row.

Under worktree-admin, after an attempted Git refusal or during repair, observable non-effects settle as terminal `Worktree { completed: false, details }` with the checked paths/registration observations, then release the candidate pin. Create requires absent registration and absent or empty owned destination; move requires absent destination plus unchanged admin identity, reciprocal source backlink and expected tip; remove requires that unchanged source state. This is record-only reconciliation under §10 rule 4, never a repeated attempt or a claim that an attempted operation was abandoned before attempt (§10 rule 4b). A replay of a false outcome returns a terminal refusal. Ambiguous residue remains pending and preserved.


Worktree WAL kinds bind canonical paths and registration names; move/remove additionally bind the admin directory's `dev:ino`, and remove binds the consumer's expected tip, delivery target and evidence digest. An established id is replayed without repeating its effect; pending attempts retain evidence. Recovery repairs a move only at its recorded destination and checks that destination's gitfile. An initializing create lock requires its own attempted WAL record, matching registration, branch and tip; a partial or dirty checkout stays preserved. Prune accepts only attempted WorktreeRemove evidence, a missing recorded checkout, the same admin inode and a matching backlink (or a partially removed backlink); it removes only the validated Git admin remainder, preserving unknown files, symlinks and native locks. It never invokes global prune or acquires custody. Four Linux x86_64 crash fixtures kill actual Git at ptrace syscall barriers; power-loss durability is not claimed.

`fgos worktree create <path> [--branch <name> | --detach] [--base <ref>] [--json]` is available now under the owner's plan Q2 answer of 2026-10-18. Without a branch it creates a detached checkout. Base accepts a full OID, HEAD or a literal branch/tag/remote ref. `fgos worktree remove <path> --delivered-to <ref> [--json]` (owner-approved 2026-10-20) wires the port's guarded remove: it resolves the worktree's current tip as `expectedTip`, resolves the delivery target (branch name, full ref or object id) to `deliveredTo`, and passes the sha256 of the delivery statement `{path, expectedTip, deliveredTo: {ref, oid}}` as `evidenceDigest`. The port refuses a dirty checkout, a live process, preserved worker state, a tip that is not an ancestor of (or equal to) `deliveredTo`, or a `deliveredTo` no non-internal ref contains; its error code and message surface unchanged and there is no force flag. Other production Worktree callers migrate together in phase 07. `git-worktree-recovery` reads raw admin entries (including partial entries omitted by Git listing), dirty/stale checkouts and pending Worktree WAL records without repairing; phase 04 adds its producing-custody row to this same diagnostic.
